bigQuestion.text: How can we make good changes in our world?

topic: Climate change: changes in the Arctic (a poem about a man and a polar bear) and clean cars.

readingSkill.name: Compare and contrast
readingSkill.bookDefinition: Compare means find the similarities, or things that are the same. Contrast means find the differences, or things that aren't the same.

pageMap.section: Unit opener: Activating Prior Knowledge About Climate Change
pageMap.contains: Title 'It Keeps Changing'. Photo: a person pours bright pink colour into a fast river. No caption.

A What do you see? ('I see a lot of pink.' 'There are so many rocks!') B What do you think? ('There's paint in the water.' 'I don't think he's safe.') C What do you wonder? ('Is it juice?' 'What is he doing?') D Think and discuss: good and bad changes in nature. E Compare and contrast a snowy setting (picture of a house in snow) to where you live. Banner: Now read The Bear and I.

pageMap.section: Reading 1 (Fiction, poem): The Bear and I - stanzas 1-2
pageMap.contains: A man from a land of wind and cold; as a young man his fishing hole was in the ice; he meets a giant arctic bear. Question: 'How many stanzas does this poem have?'

The bear is twice his size, takes his fish; for many years the bear is his enemy near his fishing hole. Label color (US) / colour (UK). Question: 'What are the dangers for the man in the poem?' Words in Context: hole, twice, enemy, thin, trap, melting.

After many warm winters the sea ice was thin; it cracked and the bear and the man fell in; they were in a trap of ice and sea together; the bear was not his enemy. Question: 'Why do you think the ice was a trap?'
Things change as years go by; danger in this changing world; today the ice is melting, the man is old and hopes to see the bear once more. Question: 'Does the man change his mind about the bear?'

pageMap.section: Explore the Reading; Social Awareness; Phonics -ng
pageMap.contains: A 5 True/False items (item 1 done: False). B Question / Answer / Stanza table (item 1 done: 'a land of wind and cold', stanza 1). C Are the man and the bear friends at the end? frame 'I think they're not friends because the bear takes his fish.' Phonics -ng: sing, long, reading, bang, spring; find more -ng words in the reading.

A check bear / man for 6 features (eats fish done for both). Definition box. B two cars (red: 'It's red and has four wheels. It's big, noisy, and fast.' white: 'This car is small, fast, and quiet. It's white and has four wheels.') circle same, underline different. C What do we use cars for? Banner: Now read Clean Cars.
Cars are everywhere; we use them to go shopping, go to school and go on vacation. Question: 'What are good and bad things about cars?'

Gasoline comes from oil in the ground; gasoline cars are fast but noisy and make the air dirty; dirty air is bad for animals, plants and people and changes our climate. Label gasoline (US) / petrol (UK). Question: 'What does your body use for energy?' Words in Context: gasoline, energy, oil, noisy, electricity, expensive.
Biofuel cars: biofuels come from plants like corn; the plants need big fields and a lot of water; the air is only a little dirty; fast but very noisy.
Electric cars use electricity like a TV or a lamp; fast and quiet; clean but expensive. Fact box: 'Electric cars aren't new. The first car to go 100 km. per hour was an electric car in 1899.'
Air cars use air for energy; not very expensive; quiet and clean but small and slow.

Solar cars use energy from the sun; some are fast; there are races; not noisy or dirty but can be expensive; not many people have them. Ending: 'Clean cars are one way to have a clean world.' Question: 'Do you like cars? Why or why not?'

A label 4 car pictures. B table Type of car / Good things / Bad things with word box fast, slow, noisy, quiet, dirty, clean, small, expensive (gasoline good: fast done). C main idea (3 options). D 'Which clean car is your favorite? Why?' frame 'I like the solar car because it's fast and quiet.'

objectives.source: added (the book does not print objectives; written from the page content)
unit: Pupils will be able to retell the poem The Bear and I in 5 simple sentences (young man, bear takes fish, thin ice, fall in, ice is melting).
Pupils will be able to compare and contrast two things (the man and the bear; two cars) using 'Both ...' and 'The bear ..., but the man ...'.
Pupils will be able to describe 5 kinds of cars (gasoline, biofuel, electric, air, solar) with fast/slow, noisy/quiet, clean/dirty, expensive.
Pupils will be able to give a reason with 'because' (I like the solar car because it's quiet.).
Pupils will be able to say one change they can make to keep the world clean (I can ... because ...).
Pupils will be able to read and say words ending in -ng (sing, long, spring, melting, fishing).
canDo: I can tell the story of the man and the bear.
I can say how two things are the same and different.
I can talk about clean cars and dirty cars.
I can say how I can help our world.
I can say words that end in -ng.
successCriteria: Sorts the 6 features on p.47 correctly (bear / man / both).
Completes the p.54 table with at least 2 good and 1 bad thing for 3 cars.
Says one 'I like ... because ...' sentence and one 'I can ... because ...' sentence.

readings.title: The Bear and I
readings.genre: Fiction - a poem (8 stanzas of 4 lines, 2 stanzas per page)
readings.speaker: a man who lives in the Arctic (he tells the story as 'I')

characters.name: the man ('I')
characters.about: young at the start, old at the end; fishes through a hole in the ice; hungry

characters.name: the polar bear
characters.about: giant, twice his size, white fur; takes his fish; hungry, just like him

readings.setting: a land of wind and cold, fields of ice and snow, the frozen sea (the Arctic)
stanzaSummaryAdded: 1 (p.42) The man is from a cold, windy land. His story starts when he was young.
2 (p.42) He fished through a hole in the ice. One day he met a giant bear.
3 (p.43) The bear was twice his size. It ate his fish, and he ran away.
4 (p.43) For many years the bear was his enemy. It was hungry, like him.
5 (p.44) After warm winters the ice was thin. It cracked and they fell in.
6 (p.44) They were in a trap of ice and sea together. The bear was not his enemy.
7 (p.45) Things change. The changing world is dangerous for them both.
8 (p.45) Today the ice is melting and the man is old. He hopes to see the bear again.

keyLinesBook.text: I'm from a land of wind and cold,
The polar bear was twice my size,
The ice on the sea was thin.
The bear was not my enemy.

causeAndEffectAdded: Thin ice → it cracked, the man and the bear fell in (p.44)
In the water together → the bear was not his enemy (p.44)
The ice is melting → danger for the bear and the man (p.45)
readings.message: Things change as years go by; the changing world is dangerous for people and animals (book p.45 idea).
